separations: Y over W/X: Y most cleanly separates definitions, causes, reforms, and the actual start of the see-also material while keeping its gists specific.
W/X over Z: Z ends with an awkward section that combines substantive methodological proposals with appendices and back matter.
articles.criterionNotes: The largest differences are in section boundaries and completeness: Y handles the sprawling article and its back matter best, while W and X make different but comparably costly grouping errors.

separations: Y over W: Y preserves the abstract/front matter division and explicitly accounts for the closing administrative material, whereas W leaves that material hidden beneath Summary.
W over X: W keeps the abstract distinct from the numbered introduction, while X incorrectly folds both into one Introduction section.
X over Z: X accurately identifies the final authorship and funding material, while Z's gist incorrectly describes it as author identities and workplaces.
articles.criterionNotes: All four track the numbered scientific sections well; they differ chiefly in completeness and boundary accuracy around the front and back matter, plus the precision of their gists.

separations: X over Z: X uses the same sound major divisions but gives more precise gists for the computational and ethical arguments.
Z over W: Z has sharper, rubric-compliant landmark titles and avoids W's overlong title for the opening argument.
W over Y: W preserves the credits as a separate division, while Y folds them into the substantive opening section.
articles.criterionNotes: The candidates mostly agree on boundaries, so titles and gist specificity decide the ranking; Y alone has a meaningful structural boundary error at the start.

separations: Z over Y: Z preserves every major argumentative turn, including visual diagnosis, formal proof, induction, mathematical counterexamples, and practical programming.
Y over W: Y correctly separates the cellular-automaton example and formal-proof discussion, which W absorbs into broader neighboring sections.
W over X: W retains the article's main conceptual progression, while X merges several distinct turns into catch-all sections.
articles.criterionNotes: Section boundaries and completeness differ most: Z mirrors the article's real sequence without sacrificing specific titles or accurate gists, while increasingly broad mergers weaken Y, W, and especially X.

separations: Z over W: Z follows the paper's actual headings throughout, while W collapses anesthesia, the hybrid framework, theory comparison, and conclusion into one catch-all.
W over X: W keeps oscillatory organization and Spatial Computing distinct and labels its closing synthesis more accurately than X.
X over Y: X preserves the abstract, introduction, and classical-model setup, whereas Y compresses nearly all of that foundation into one oversized section.
articles.criterionNotes: The decisive criterion is structural completeness: Z captures each substantive division with specific, accurate gists, while the others progressively flatten or merge the paper's argument.

separations: Y over Z: Y gives the notes their own clean section instead of nesting them beneath the concluding argument, while retaining all of the essay's major case-study divisions.
Z over X: Z more clearly separates the article metadata from the relational-future thesis and gives especially specific gists for the historical cases.
X over W: X describes the aristocratic case as a contrast with work, while W inaccurately suggests those lives lacked meaning rather than locating meaning in relational status.
articles.criterionNotes: All four recognize the essay's five-part argument, but nesting of the notes, the opening boundary, and gist accuracy distinguish them.

separations: Y over W/Z: Y combines the shared clean structure with the most specific and comprehensive gists, especially for silk types, artificial production, and human applications.
W/Z over X: W and Z preserve more discriminating scientific and historical detail, while X's gists are consistently more generic.
articles.criterionNotes: The section boundaries and completeness are essentially identical, so the ranking turns chiefly on title usefulness and gist specificity.

separations: Z over X: Z preserves X's coherent argumentative grouping while giving Feynman's final wish its own proper closing section.
X over W: X places the cargo-cult metaphor together with the integrity principle it introduces, whereas W leaves the defining metaphor in the preceding pseudoscience survey.
W over Y: W provides a complete, usable hierarchy, while Y produced no usable output.
articles.criterionNotes: The main difference is where the central conceptual turn occurs: Z and X place it at the definition of Cargo Cult Science, while W delays the boundary until the explanation of scientific integrity.
